lines.text: Does feeling rejected prove you were rejected?
Treating a feeling as proof is called emotional reasoning.
Researchers gave people short stories about everyday situations.
Some stories added one detail: the person in them felt anxious.
Of one hundred eighty-six people, those with anxiety disorders saw more danger just because of that feeling.
The others judged by the facts alone.
A feeling is real information about you.
It just isn't always proof about the world.

post.title: Your Feelings Aren't Always Facts #shorts
post.description: Feeling it doesn't make it true. Arntz, Rauner & van den Hout (1995) found people with anxiety disorders rated situations as more dangerous when the story said the person felt anxious, even when the facts said safe; people without anxiety disorders went by the facts. Psychologists call it emotional reasoning. #psychology #emotions #mentalhealth
